clue.text: Cut throat

definitions.meaning: to cut short, as hair or grass
a bird's ... is the pouch in its gullet, part of the throat

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are standard: the verb for trimming short and the noun for a bird's food pouch in the gullet.

clue.text: Items to discuss? Get on with new one after Director intervenes

indicators.note: something that intervenes comes between other things, so the director's letter is placed within the run

parts.note: to get on in years is to age
A means one, as in a single thing

explanation.surface: A chair urges the meeting to press on with a fresh list of points once the director has butted in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'intervenes' puts D between the N and the A of AGE+N+A.
explanation.definitionFit: A meeting's agenda is its list of business, the matters people will discuss.

clue.text: Futile debut of one very much sent up during match

indicators.note: a debut is a first appearance, so only the opening letter of the word one is used
the reversed letters fall during, that is inside, the match word

parts.note: a tie is a match or fixture, as in a cup tie

indicators.note: in a down clue, sent up means the word is written bottom to top, read backwards

parts.note: so means very much, as in 'so tired'

explanation.surface: A newcomer's first game ends in futility when they are mocked mid-match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sent up' fits a down clue: the letters for 'very much' are read upwards before going into the match word.
explanation.definitionFit: Otiose is a formal synonym for pointless or serving no purpose.

clue.text: God leading South American people to North America — an epic story

indicators.note: leading means coming first, so the god's letters head the answer

parts.note: Ra is the Egyptian sun god
the Maya are a people of Central America, loosely placed here as South American

explanation.surface: Reads like the plot of a migration saga: a deity guides a people northward.
explanation.definitionFit: The Ramayana is the great Sanskrit epic poem telling the story of Rama.

clue.text: Jabber in chirpy mode, excitedly

indicators.note: doing something excitedly means in an agitated, jumbled way, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone chatters away cheerfully and excitedly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jabber' looks like a verb for chattering; here it is a thing that jabs, a needle.
explanation.definitionFit: A hypodermic needle jabs the skin, so it is jokingly a jabber.

clue.text: Exploit story, dismissing articles in fine condition

indicators.note: dismissing means sending away, so the article letters are removed

parts.note: a feat is a notable exploit or deed
a tale is a story
a is the indefinite article, so two articles give two letter As

explanation.surface: A tale of heroic deeds is trimmed of its little words and left in good shape.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dismissing' takes both As out of FEATTALE.
explanation.definitionFit: Fettle means state or trim, and especially good form, as in the idiom about being in fine shape.

clue.text: Blazing about Republican, OK?

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the blazing word goes round the Republican letter

parts.note: something blazing is alight, on fire

explanation.surface: Someone checks on a fiery Republican politician: everything fine?
explanation.definitionFit: The informal spelling of all right means OK or satisfactory.

clue.text: Meets a club host over in front of system

parts.note: the DJ hosts the music at a nightclub
O is the cricket scoring abbreviation for an over

indicators.note: the front of a word is its first letter, so only the opening of system is used

explanation.surface: A nightclub DJ is introduced before the sound system is set up.
explanation.definitionFit: Two things that adjoin touch or border each other, so they meet.

clue.text: Valued return of my drug, alas

parts.note: something valued is dear to you

indicators.note: a return goes back the way it came, so the word my is read backwards

parts.note: E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: Someone laments getting back an expensive stash of drugs.
explanation.definitionFit: Dear me is an old-fashioned exclamation of dismay, like oh dear.

clue.text: Swindled daughter? Was not greatly exercised about daughter

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the idle verb goes round the second D

parts.note: a person or engine that idled was not working hard
D abbreviates daughter again

explanation.surface: A parent wonders if their daughter was cheated, and frets that they were not upset enough about it.
explanation.definitionFit: To diddle is a colloquial verb for cheating someone, so diddled means conned.

clue.text: Varnish apparently secured in early part of year

indicators.note: secured in means held inside, so these letters sit within the month

parts.note: Jan, January, is the start of the year
ap. is a dictionary abbreviation for apparent or apparently

explanation.surface: Varnish has seemingly been locked in place early in the year.
explanation.definitionFit: Japan is a hard black lacquer, named after the country where the technique began.

clue.text: Leftover amount, it seems

parts.note: read the answer as wordplay: an odd, rearranged version of MAN OUT spells the clue word amount

explanation.surface: A spare quantity, apparently.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it seems' says the clue word is what the answer would produce if read as an instruction.
explanation.definitionFit: The one left over after pairing up is the one who doesn't fit in.

clue.text: Condition limiting new game leads to anger

indicators.note: leads to sets the first part ahead of the second
limiting means enclosing, so the condition word goes round the new letter

parts.note: if introduces a condition
a game leg is lame, injured

explanation.surface: A rule cap on a new game provokes fury.
explanation.definitionFit: To inflame is to stir up passion or rage in someone, provoking them.

clue.text: Just one room popular? Dull to accept that

indicators.note: to accept is to take in, so the dull word holds the other letters

parts.note: colours that have faded are dull
I is the Roman numeral one
in means fashionable or popular

explanation.surface: Is a single room enough to keep everyone happy? It seems dull to go along with it.
explanation.definitionFit: A just person is impartial, judging fairly without bias.

clue.text: Don't mess with first two characters variously interrupting reception

indicators.note: interrupting means breaking into, so each letter is placed inside the reception word
variously says the two letters go in at different places rather than as a pair

parts.note: a levee is a formal reception, originally held by a monarch on rising
the first two characters of the alphabet are A and B; first supplies the opening one, A
the second of the first two alphabet characters is B

explanation.surface: A warning not to meddle with the opening pair who keep disrupting a party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first two characters' are A and B; 'variously interrupting' puts them into LEVEE at separate points, LE-A-VE-B-E.
explanation.definitionFit: To let something alone is an idiom for not interfering with it.

clue.text: Indicator of amusement I extracted from comparison

indicators.note: extracted from means taken out, so the letter I is removed

parts.note: a simile is a figure of speech making a comparison

explanation.surface: Reads like a literary analysis pulling a sign of humour out of a comparison.
explanation.definitionFit: A grin or upturned mouth shows that someone is amused.

clue.text: Retired? Time sure flies

indicators.note: letters that fly about are scattered, so these are rearranged

explanation.surface: A retiree musing on how quickly the years pass.
explanation.definitionFit: Emeritus describes a professor who has retired but keeps the title; the question mark flags the narrow sense.

clue.text: Really good pop group ditching name

indicators.note: ditching means dropping, so the name letter is removed

parts.note: a band is a pop group

explanation.surface: An excellent band that has dropped its name.
explanation.definitionFit: In slang, bad can mean excellent, the reverse of its usual sense.

clue.text: Crazy series penned by idiot

indicators.note: penned by means enclosed by, so the idiot word goes round the series letters

parts.note: berk is British slang for a fool

explanation.surface: A mad series of books written by a fool.
explanation.definitionFit: Going berserk means wild or frenzied, out of control.

clue.text: Own a former European currency — Italian?

parts.note: DM is the Deutschmark, Germany's currency before the euro

explanation.surface: Is that old European money really Italian?
explanation.definitionFit: To own up, or own, is to confess or acknowledge something.

clue.text: Sailor understands aims

parts.note: tar is an old word for a sailor
if you get something you understand it

explanation.surface: A sailor grasps the objectives.
explanation.definitionFit: Aims and goals are things one sets out to hit, plural nouns matching the answer.

clue.text: Host runs last equal

indicators.note: last tells us the runs letter goes to the end of the word

parts.note: a compere hosts a show
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A show's presenter comes in last, equal with others.
explanation.walkthrough: 'runs last' moves the R of COMPERE to the end.
explanation.definitionFit: A compeer is a peer or companion of the same standing.

clue.text: Orator curtailed boast, retaining reserve

indicators.note: retaining means holding within, so the shortened word goes round the reserve word
curtailed means having its tail cut off, so the last letter goes

parts.note: to crow is to boast
ice means reserve, coolness of manner

explanation.surface: A speaker cuts short his bragging and keeps his cool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'curtailed' cuts CROW to CRO, which holds ICE.
explanation.definitionFit: Cicero was the celebrated Roman statesman and public speaker.

clue.text: US coach to scoff about rule

parts.note: to rail is to jeer or complain scornfully
ca. (circa) means about

explanation.surface: An American trainer mocks a regulation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coach' suggests a sports trainer; it is a railway carriage.
explanation.definitionFit: In American usage a railcar is a railway carriage, which British English also calls a coach.

clue.text: Selling last of ale and port in bar, …

indicators.note: in places the end letters inside the bar word

parts.note: a rail is a bar

indicators.note: the last of each word is its final letter, taken from both ale and port

explanation.surface: Selling beer and wine at a pub counter.
explanation.definitionFit: Retail is the selling of goods directly to the public.

clue.text: … wild scene finally after pub restricts it

indicators.note: after places the scene letter at the end
restricts means confines, so the pub word goes round the it letters

parts.note: an inn is a pub
it means sex appeal, abbreviated SA

indicators.note: finally points to the last letter of scene

explanation.surface: Continues the bar picture: a wild scene breaks out at closing when the pub clamps down.
explanation.definitionFit: Crazy, wild and insane are synonyms for out of one's mind or reckless.

clue.text: Most restrained since cost exploded

indicators.note: exploded means blown apart, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Restraint is at its peak since the cost has rocketed.
explanation.definitionFit: Concise means brief and economical, so its superlative is the most restrained in wording.

clue.text: Swordsman recalled times around capital of Bulgaria

indicators.note: around means surrounding, so the reversed word goes round the Bulgarian letter
recalled means called back, so the times word is read backwards

parts.note: eras are periods of time

indicators.note: the capital of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A fencer reminisces about times spent in Sofia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recalled' makes SARE from ERAS. 'capital of Bulgaria' tempts SOFIA; it is just B.
explanation.definitionFit: A sabre is a soldier armed with a sword, as a cavalryman, by metonymy.

clue.text: John pens 50 comments online?

indicators.note: pens means encloses, so the toilet word goes round the fifty letter

parts.note: john and bog are both slang for a toilet
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: A man named John writes fifty online comments.
explanation.walkthrough: 'John' looks like a name; it is US slang for a toilet, BOG in British slang.
explanation.definitionFit: A blog is a website of a writer's posts and remarks, with a question mark as a loose description.

clue.text: Eggs upset deer

parts.note: roe is the mass of eggs in a fish
a horse that bucks throws or upsets its rider

explanation.surface: Some eggs disturbed a deer.
explanation.definitionFit: A roebuck is the male roe deer.

clue.text: One with good sense, storing energy of volcanic rock

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: storing means keeping inside, so the sense word holds the energy letter

parts.note: nous is common sense
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A sensible person stores up power from the volcano.
explanation.definitionFit: Igneous describes rock formed from cooled magma, as from volcanoes.
